title: Integer range and factorial
text: A signed 32-bit int represents -2147483648 to 2147483647. Factorial fits for inputs 0 through 12. Define the input contract and check larger inputs explicitly. A signed overflow finding is different from a wrong-output finding.

title: Preconditions and postconditions
text: A function contract identifies valid inputs and the required result. Check equal and boundary values. For a maximum function, equal arguments must return that same value. For factorial, zero factorial equals one.

title: Checking C input
text: Check the return value of scanf before using a variable. Define array-size limits before allocation. Invalid or absent input may terminate main before the intended algorithm executes.

title: Understanding verification limits
text: A KLEE timeout is inconclusive. A CBMC unwinding failure indicates that the selected bound was insufficient for that claim. SAT on a KLEE path query shows query satisfiability and is not by itself a program failure.

title: Unsigned 64-bit range and factorial
text: For a 64-bit unsigned long long, values range from 0 to 18446744073709551615. 20! equals 2432902008176640000 and fits; 21! exceeds this range. A guarded input domain of 0 through 20 is appropriate for this representation. The signed 32-bit limit of 12! applies to an int factorial, not this unsigned 64-bit accumulator.
